caption:
Swipe to see what Anthropic's own economic model says about your job by 2030. 👇

The model covers AI's impact on jobs, wages, and economic growth through 2030 across three scenarios, a survey of 10,000+ Americans on what they expect, and a live comparison tool at anthropic.com where you stack your prediction against everyone else's. 8.8 million people have already clicked, which is the number that makes the whole thing feel different.

Anthropicbuilt the AI. Then they built the tool that maps out how it might hurt your paycheck. When the company causing the disruption starts modeling its own damage in detail, that's not a reassurance. That's a confirmation. The fear is real enough to quantify now.

Running a business? DM us "AI" and we'll show you what this means for your workforce before your competitors figure it out.

Sources: Anthropic, X (AnthropicAI)

pinned_comment: Would you trust a model about AI job losses if the company building the AI made the model? That's exactly what 8.8 million people just did.

candidates: THE COMPANY BUILDING AI LET 10,000 AMERICANS PREDICT WHAT IT DOES TO THEIR JOB BY 2030. NOW YOU CAN SEE WHERE YOU LAND.
THE COMPANY MAKING THE AI ASKED YOU TO PREDICT YOUR OWN ECONOMIC FUTURE BECAUSE OF IT, AND 8.8 MILLION DID
THE COMPANY BUILDING AI JUST PUBLISHED ITS OWN MODEL ON WHAT HAPPENS TO YOUR JOB BY 2030. THEN IT ASKED 10,000 WORKERS IF THEY AGREE.
hook_tournament.why: [2] creates a two-act story (prediction published, workers respond) that makes you want to know what happens next, while [0] just promises a personal ranking. Stories hook harder than interactive quizzes for stop-scrolling.

candidates: THE COMPANY BUILDING AI JUST PUBLISHED ITS OWN MODEL ON WHAT HAPPENS TO YOUR JOB BY 2030. THEN IT ASKED 10,000 WORKERS IF THEY AGREE.

hook_sharpen.why: "PREDICT THEIR OWN FATE" is ominous where "agree" is procedural. The word "WAGES" makes it concrete fear, not abstract model-talk.
